meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil law codified framework with Sharia influences; modern commercial law modeled partially on English common-law principles)

Oman-GCC Unified Economic Agreement (includes GCC members)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Royal Decree 30/2016 (Commercial Companies Law, as amended by RD 66/2020); Royal Decree 31/2019 (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Law); CBO AML/CFT Regulations (Circular BM 1108 and subsequent CBO rules); Royal Decree 54/2021 (Beneficial Ownership Information Regulations, implementing amendments to Commercial Companies Law requiring UBO filings in the Commercial Register); Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MOCIIP) Beneficial Ownership Register; Oman Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) regulations, guidance and reporting standards; Oman Capital Market Authority AML/CFT provisions for licensed capital-market entities; Royal Decree 45/2021 (Strategic Goods Control Law) for defense/dual-use goods manufacturing; associated implementing regulations and licensing procedures.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced screening of all UBOs, managers, directors, and authorized signatories against: (i) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List; (iii) UK HM Treasury Sanctions List; (iv) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (v) Oman Financial Intelligence Unit domestic lists; (vi) Interpol Red Notices; (vii) World Bank / EBRD debarment lists; (viii) GCC anti-terrorism lists; and (ix) adverse media and PEP databases. Full-profile mandatory screening is required pre-incorporation, with enhanced due diligence (EDD) triggered if any UBO, manager or beneficial owner is a politically exposed person (PEP), a family member or close associate of a PEP, or connected to a sanctioned jurisdiction. Positive screening results — including potential exact or fuzzy matches — must be escalated to the Oman FIU under the AML/CFT law and will require a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) filing prior to any incorporation filing. Failure to perform screening constitutes a predicate violation under the Oman AML/CFT Law and can expose the Omani licensed law firm or corporate service provider to criminal liability, fines, and suspension.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MOCIIP) Commercial Registry e-Services portal (invest.om / commercialregistry.om electronic services; also accessible through 'Invest in Oman' national investment portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Legal-entity names in Oman must be registered in Arabic as the primary script. English transliteration may be filed as a secondary trade name provided it is a direct phonetic/literal transliteration of the Arabic name, without meaning alteration. Trade names must conform to Islamic and GCC conventions; any foreign word, if used, must be transliterated into Arabic alphabet and the English version is entirely supplementary. Statutory name doctrine requires inclusion of the legal-form indicator — 'ذات مسئولية محدودة بشخص واحد' (limited liability single person company) or 'SPC' — and must be capable of distinguishing the entity from any registered company, trademark, or public-interest name. Foreign-字母 trade names are accepted only in the transliterated format; expansion of acronyms or artificial lettering is prohibited unless MOCIIP grants a special exemption.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Anything implying affiliation with the Omani Government or abroad-government sponsorship without prior ministerial consent
Words contrary to public order, religious sensitivities, or public morals
Any misleading indication of prohibited business purposes
Terms implying military/defense manufacturing without Ministry of Defense or Strategic Goods Control approval
Terms suggesting the manufacture of weapons of mass destruction or dual-use biological/chemical materials
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration request through the same MOCIIP e-service portal within 15 working days from the rejection notification, attaching supporting trademark certificates or Arabic name-evidence. If the reconsideration is denied, a formal administrative appeal may be lodged before the MOCIIP Appeals Committee within 30 days of the reconsideration decision. A further appeal may be filed with the Omani Administrative Court / Court of First Instance under the Code of Administrative Procedure within 60 days of the final administrative refusal. Parallel re-application with a new name is permitted at any time, but the original reservation fee is not refundable and a new name-search fee applies. Name reservation validity of 30 days may be renewed on payment of a standard extension fee for an additional 30-day period, after which a new reservation request must be filed. Name clearance is not final until incorporation has been completed; MOCIIP may cancel a reserved name if the underlying incorporation is not completed within the reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for a manufacturing company engaged in ISIC 3040 military tactical vehicle production. Oman law requires the SPC to have a physical registered office located in the Sultanate, evidenced by a valid tenancy contract (Ejari-registered) or title deed, and the offices must be the actual site where the company operates, maintains registers, and receives government correspondence. A pure virtual office address is likely to be rejected for this defense-sector manufacturing scope. However, a serviced office or business center address may be permissible in the short pre-incorporation stage to obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, but the industrial license phase requires a physical manufacturing site and operational premises, and MOCIIP / Ministry of Defense / Royal Oman Police may condition issuance of licenses on actual operating premises. Commercial substance requirements apply on an ongoing basis: payroll, management decisions, factory floor operations, storage of key records, and essential administrative functions must be located in Oman.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (85% probability within the first 12 months after incorporation). Defense and dual-use manufacturing is expressly high-risk; Oman's Strategic Goods Control Directorate, Ministry of Defense, Royal Oman Police, and MOCIIP undertake unannounced inspections to verify physical substance, security of facilities, existence of actual manufacturing equipment, storage of controlled materials, export compliance systems, and UBO continuity. The company should expect an on-site inspection within the initial license period, and in many cases before final approval of the military/defense production license.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Oman Commercial Companies Law, Royal Decree No. 18/2019, as amended; applicable provisions on the Single Person Company (Articles 65–78), the commercial registration regime, and the implementing ministerial decisions issued by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) – Directorate General of Commerce, Companies Registration Department; nationwide electronic filing through the Invest in Oman portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation application in the prescribed SPC format, together with the notarized Articles of Association and Commercial Registry registration form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an SPC under the Commercial Companies Law; however, for defense-sector manufacturing, the Ministry of Defence and industrial licensing authorities generally require a paid-up share capital of at least OMR 1,000,000, deposited in a licensed commercial bank in Oman. The share capital must be fully subscribed and certified by a banker's deposit certificate before final license issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the sole member of OM SPC LLC, that: (1) the company is formed under Royal Decree No. 18/2019 as a Single Person Company, subscribed at OMR 1,000,000, and the capital deposit certificate shall be delivered to the Commercial Registrar; (2) the registered office is fixed at the premises described in the Articles of Association, Muscat Governorate, Sultanate of Oman; (3) the following officers are appointed: [Name] as Managing Director and [Name] as Secretary, with authority to sign all registration forms, open bank accounts, appoint auditors, and obtain industrial, defense, and environmental approvals; and (4) any previous instructions conflicting with this resolution are revoked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Legal Form Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MoCIIP – Directorate General of Trade Registration through the Invest in Oman e-portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application to reserve the trade name 'OM SPC LLC' and to confirm the Single Person Company legal form for the specified defense manufacturing scope. The system checks name uniqueness and compatibility with ISIC 3040. Pay the name reservation fee and download the official reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Passport copy of the sole shareholder/beneficial owner
No-objection letter from the Ministry of Defence for the use of defense-related terminology in the trade name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of rejection, file a written reconsideration request with the MoCIIP Name Committee within 14 days or submit an amended name with a distinctive identifier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public licensed by the MoCIIP in the Muscat Governorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a locally licensed advocate to draft the SPC Articles of Association in Arabic, specifying the sole member, share capital, registered office, and authorized business activities encompassing armored security personnel transport vehicle manufacturing. Execute the document before the notary public and complete the attestation formalities required by the registrar.
required_dossiers: Valid civil ID or passport copy of the sole shareholder
Power of attorney, if signing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is queried, correct the deficiency and re-execute before the notary; any erroneous stamp duty is refundable by the Notary Office upon submission of the corrected instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Capital Escrow Account and Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in the Sultanate of Oman, subject to Central Bank of Oman regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account under the proposed company name and deposit the stated paid-up capital, or secure an irrevocable bank undertaking if the capital is to be called in stages. Obtain a banker's certificate confirming the deposit and account opening details; retain the certificate for submission to the Commercial Registrar.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry preliminary approval or name reservation certificate
Shareholder identification documents and beneficial ownership declaration
Board resolution authorizing the bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence due to the defense-related business scope, submit a supplementary declaration of beneficial ownership and source of funds; the bank must issue the certificate within 10 working days after compliance, or another licensed bank may be engaged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to the Commercial Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MoCIIP – Commercial Registrar through the Invest in Oman e-portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized Articles of Association, capital deposit certificate, consent of the audit firm, and the lease agreement for the registered office. Pay the commercial registration fee. The Registrar verifies the SPC structure, capital, and statutory prerequisites, and issues the Commercial Registration Certificate for OM SPC LLC.
required_dossiers: Capital deposit certificate or bank undertaking
Board appointment form and officer ID copies
Negative fit-and-proper declaration for a defense contractor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query, respond through the portal within 10 working days; if the Articles of Association require amendment, re-notarize and resubmit, and the application clock shall be extended by a further 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oman Tax Authority and Public Authority for Social Insurance (PASI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Commercial Registration Certificate, complete the tax registration with the Oman Tax Authority to secure the Tax Identification Number and Employer Registration Number, and register with PASI for future employee social insurance obligations. Verify that the defense-related income will be treated under the standard corporate tax regime.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed or queried, submit an amendment application with an explanatory cover letter and the Commercial Registration Certificate to the Oman Tax Authority registration desk; the file is to be corrected within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry Membership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OCCI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated SPC with OCCI and pay the annual membership fee. Obtain the OCCI membership certificate, which is required for import permits, government procurement, and certain industrial licensing procedures.
required_dossiers: Shareholder civil ID or passport copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the OCCI application is returned, rectify any discrepancy in the commercial registration and resubmit; delayed membership is curable by payment of the annual fee and presentation of a certified CR extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MoCIIP – Industrial Development Directorate, with compulsory consultation of the Ministry of Defence – Defence Procurement Board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for an Industrial Manufacturing License covering 'Manufacture of Armored Security Personnel Transport Vehicles' under ISIC 3040. Provide the facility technical file, security clearances for shareholders and directors, and compliance with the Defense Contractor Eligibility Criteria. The Ministry of Defence must issue the defense contractor eligibility certificate before MoCIIP will grant the industrial license.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Certificate and OCCI membership
Detailed project technical report and production equipment list
Facility layout drawing and security plan
Beneficial ownership declarations and security clearance forms
Civil Defense and fire safety pre-approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license application is queried, respond to the clarifications within 30 days, address defense security concerns in a revised security plan, and re-submit to the Industrial Development Directorate; denial may be appealed to the Ministerial Industrial Appeals Committee within 21 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Premises, Environmental, and Operational License Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Muscat Municipality, Framework for Civil Defence and Ambulance Authority, and the Environment Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the on-site inspection of the production facility, the structural load certification, the civil defense fire safety sign-off, and the environmental compliance validation. After final approvals, the registry records the operational home-possession status and activates the CR for commercial operations.
required_dossiers: Waste management and industrial wastewater disposal contract
Civil Defense and Ministry of Labour workplace clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cite minor deficiencies and cure them within 10 working days; request a reinspection with the inspecting authority. If a substantial nonconformity exists, submit a corrective action plan and undergo a follow-up inspection before the license is activated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) – Industrial Development Directorate, jointly with the Ministry of Defence – Defence Procurement Board for defense contractor eligibility
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Defense Manufacturing Industrial License (Special Industrial License for Manufacture of Armored Security Personnel Transport Vehicles, ISIC 3040)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 1 – Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report required due to metal fabrication, welding, painting, and hazardous waste generation in the armored vehicle production process.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Omani Air Quality Standards under Ministerial Decision No. 79/2014; industrial wastewater must meet the treated effluent discharge standards under Ministerial Decision No. 145/1993; VOC emission controls must apply best available techniques (BAT) and hazardous waste must be transported and disposed of only through Environment Authority-licensed waste operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Royal Oman Police – Civil Defence and Ambulance Authority; structural load inspection certificate issued by a licensed civil engineer; occupational health and safety clearance from the Ministry of Labour; and workplace authorization for the production facility meeting the Facility Code for Defense Manufacturing sites.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Oman Tax Authority (OTA), successor to the Secretariat General for Taxation, Ministry of Finance; national e-filing portal: https://etax.taxoman.gov.om (eTax). Customs administration is vested in the Directorate General of Customs of the Royal Oman Police (ROP Customs); foreign investment and commercial registration are administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP); military hardware licensing is overseen by the Ministry of Defence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Oman (CBO). Foreign exchange control, supervision of licensed banks, and cross-border payment system oversight are exercised by the CBO under the Banking Law, the Foreign Exchange Regulations, and the AML/CFT Law. Regulatory coordination for foreign investment registration is shared with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Omani Rial is fully convertible at the official pegged rate of 1 OMR = 2.60028 USD. Current account transactions, including trade-related cross-border payments and service fees, are generally unrestricted and processed by licensed banks after standard AML/KYC scrutiny. Capital account flows, including inbound equity injection and foreign direct investment for a 100% foreign-owned Single Person Company, are permissible without general CBO prior approval but require compliance with foreign investment registration, commercial registration, and beneficial ownership disclosure. Profit remittances require audited financial statements, proof of distributable earnings, verification of tax settlement with the Oman Tax Authority, and submission of standard bank remittance declarations. OMR is not a deliverable offshore currency outside the GCC clearing framework in practice, so most international clearing is settled in USD through CBO-regulated correspondent banking channels.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Oman does not impose a statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Exporters may keep export receipts in foreign currency in a licensed foreign currency account or convert to OMR at the prevailing market rate. There is no prescribed CBO timeline for converting export proceeds; however, banks require inward remittance advices and underlying export documentation (commercial invoice, bill of lading, customs declaration, and the relevant CBO balance-of-payments reporting code) to classify the receipt. For defense and tactical hardware exports, the export-import license issued by the competent Omani authorities and the end-user certificate must accompany the transaction to avoid AML/export-control holds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational USD & OMR Current Account
Capital Escrow Account / Correspondent USD Account / Trade LC Account
Operational Current Account / Export Proceeds Account
Operational Current Account / Government Contract Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI and virtual payment accounts are not recognized by the CBO as regulated clearing institutions. Any payment service provider or electronic money institution operating in Oman must be licensed by the CBO and maintain a physical or agency arrangement with a licensed Omani bank. For an ISIC 3040 defense-tactical business, fintech EMIs are legally unsuitable as the primary clearing rail and pose an unacceptable concentration risk; they can only be used as ancillary payment interfaces where the underlying settlement remains with a tier-1 licensed Omani bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the high-risk defense manufacturing classification. The SPC's legal representative, each director, and the ultimate beneficial owner must attend an in-person KYC interview at the Omani bank's designated branch in Oman, present original passports, valid residency or commercial registration documents, and sign the bank's declaration of ultimate beneficial ownership, source of funds, and intended transaction profile. CBO's enhanced due diligence expectations for defense-related entities do not permit purely remote or video-KYC onboarding for the initial account opening; remote documentary submission may only be considered for subsequent account operations after the initial in-person relationship is established.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector classification of armored military vehicle manufacturing triggering enhanced due diligence, defense-sector red flags, and possible proliferation finance screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory commercial registration; Oman Chamber of Commerce membership; Ministry of Commerce license for ISIC 3040; Ministry of Defense import-export authorization; end-user certificate; final destination undertaking; corporate compliance manual addressing export controls, sanctions screening, and defense procurement; and a board resolution defining the lawful manufacturing and sales purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership in a 100% foreign-owned SPC with non-resident shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Memorandum and Articles of Association; full SPC incorporation certificate; bank-verified register of shareholders and directors; UBO declaration form; passport copies and proof of residential address of each UBO; parent company audit report; reference letters from the foreign parent's regulated bank; and prior corporate tax registration evidence from the Oman Tax Authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually large inbound government or diplomatic wires requiring immediate clearing, coupled with possible restricted destination or strategic goods exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed government procurement contract or diplomatic purchase order; matching invoices and packing lists; signed source-of-funds declaration; identity and mandate documents of the counterparty signatory; official confirmation from the paying ministry or embassy; end-user and end-use certificate; delivery terms and transport documents; and full SWIFT flow transparency to avoid layering.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound trade disbursements to foreign intermediary or defense component suppliers triggering sanctions and trade control red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete contract chain from prime contractor to each supplier; intermediary license where applicable; validated export licenses for all military and dual-use items; supplier KYC pack; bank references; payment milestone schedule; letters of non-reshipping and no-retransfer; confirmation that neither the bank, the counterparty, nor the transit states appear on sanctioned-party lists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer from the foreign parent account to the SPC's capital escrow account maintained at the Omani bank. The payment narrative must clearly state 'SHARE CAPITAL INJECTION' and reference the SPC commercial registration and capital subscription resolution. Banks will map the transaction to the CBO balance-of-payments code for inward direct investment in a nonresident-owned enterprise. Verification includes the foreign parent's audited financial statement, bank source-of-funds confirmation, shareholder registers, and the Oman MOIIP foreign investment registration certificate. The funds may be credited as OMR if the parent uses its own FX; alternatively, the Omani bank can convert the USD at the pegged rate after deduction of normal FX spreads. No CBO exchange control approval is required where the remittance is for an allowed capital entry purpose and passes AML/KYC scrutiny.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement uses established bank clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments on confirmed invoices; (b) MT202 for bank-to-bank USD credit transfers where intermediary banks are involved; (c) commercial documentary letters of credit issued by the Omani bank and advised through MT700, with sight or usance payment against presentation of shipping/warehouse documents; (d) collections under MT799/MT400-style instructions for DP/DA transactions where LC is not required. For all defense-related outbound payments, the bank will require the export license, end-user certificate, commercial invoice, proof of delivery terms, and transaction-level sanctions screening. OMR is not normally used for cross-border trade clearing; USD is the preferred settlement currency through the CBO-regulated bank's nostro network.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with a CBO-licensed commercial bank for USD/OMR and major trade currencies, limited to bona fide current or capital transaction exposure.
Plain vanilla FX options with a licensed bank to hedge foreign currency procurement or export payment volatility.
Cross-currency swaps between USD and OMR for long-term capital/financing hedging, executed on an OTC basis with regulated counterparties.

Non-deliverable forwards are permissible only where offered by an authorized intermediary as an offshore risk-management tool for a non-deliverable currency; because OMR is pegged and tradable onshore, NDF use is not normally required and may be disfavored by Omani regulators for purely speculative purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Register Renewal and Confirmation Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Directorate, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion, Sultanate of Oman
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the anniversary of the commercial registration certificate issuance date; a 30-day grace period is available before late penalties accrue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs OMR 10 per week up to OMR 300; commercial registration is suspended after 30 days past grace; non-renewal for 90 days triggers strike-off procedures and potential compulsory liquidation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion, Sultanate of Oman
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end (for a 31 December year-end, submit by 30 June of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file audited financial statements within the prescribed period exposes the SPC to a warning followed by a fine of OMR 500–1,500 under the Omani Commercial Companies Law; continued non-compliance may lead to suspension of the commercial registration and dissolution by court order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Annual Confirmation and Shareholding Transfer Notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Beneficial Ownership Register, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion, Sultanate of Oman
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation filed together with the commercial register renewal; any change in beneficial ownership arising from a share transfer must be notified within 14 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or misstatement of beneficial ownership information subjects the SPC to administrative fines of OMR 1,000–3,000 under the AML implementing regulations and to temporary suspension of the company's legal personality

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Assembly Filing and Statutory Register Audit Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with a governmental authority; minutes and resolutions are retained in the statutory minute book and made available to the Registrar on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General meeting must be convened within 4 months following the financial year-end; auditor appointment and annual accounts approval must be recorded in the minutes by no later than 30 June for a 31 December fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the general meeting or to maintain audited statutory records exposes the board and the single partner to fines under the Commercial Companies Law and to judicial supervision upon the Registrar's petition

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Omani commercial companies, including Single Person Companies owned by non-residents, are required to appoint a certified auditor and submit audited financial statements annually; no turnover or balance-sheet exemption is available for foreign-owned defense-tactical manufacturing SPCs
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and officially adopted by the Sultanate of Oman; supplementary disclosure obligations arise from the Omani Commercial Companies Law and the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion's financial reporting directives

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SPC must maintain a current Beneficial Owner Register and confirm the accuracy of that register with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion on an annual basis; any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 14 days of occurrence, and a copy of the updated register must be retained at the Omani registered office

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–1,500 per year for an Oman registered agent and office address service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500–4,000 per year for an IFRS audit of a defense-tactical manufacturing SPC

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (flat headline corporate rate; SME taxpayers benefit from progressive rates: 0% up to OMR 30,000; 3% OMR 30,001-100,000; 5% OMR 100,001-200,000; 7.5% OMR 200,001-300,000; 10% OMR 300,001-500,000; 12.5% OMR 500,001-1,000,000; 15% above OMR 1,000,000).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying strategic manufacturing projects (including armored/defense vehicle production) approved by the Oman Investment Authority may receive a corporate income tax holiday of up to 5 years under the Investment Law, extendable to up to 10 years for projects of high national value; customs duty exemptions are available on capital equipment imports; 0% rate applies to the first OMR 30,000 of taxable income for SME-qualifying entities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: OTA Corporate Income Tax Return e-Form, filed electronically through the Oman Tax Authority (OTA) e-Services Portal (https://taxoman.gov.om); audited financial statements and tax computation must be uploaded as attachments; the return is accepted in Arabic with bilingual forms permitted.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Large taxpayers (prior-year assessed tax exceeding OMR 1,000,000) must also file quarterly advance income tax instalment declarations with payments due on 31 July, 31 October, 31 January and 30 April.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the end of the accounting period; for a 31 December fiscal year-end the statutory filing and payment deadline is 30 April; a one-month extension may be granted upon written application to the OTA before the due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial Registration (CR) number issued by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion and the OTA-issued Tax Identification Number (TIN) allocated to the SPC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not complete this Box; the SPC must input its own Omani CR/TIN; foreign ownership percentage and shareholder identity must be reflected in the attached ownership schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Accounting Period and Tax Residency
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the tax period; confirmation that the SPC is resident in Oman by virtue of incorporation and place of effective management (POEM).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If foreign management exercises substantive decisions outside Oman, POEM relocation risk arises; attach board minutes, management meeting logs and decision records to evidence Omani substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross invoiced revenue from sale of all-terrain military tactical vehicles, spare parts, technical after-sales services and government export contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Export sales must be supported by title-transfer and risk-passing evidence; government/diplomatic-letter-of-credit transactions are reportable at FOB/CIF invoice values.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Cost of Goods Sold and Capital Allowances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct material and labour, factory overheads and statutory depreciation/capital allowances on industrial machinery and production facilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Defense-related technical IP acquired from foreign affiliates must be arm's length priced; all royalty and cost allocations require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Taxable Adjustments and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses (fines, unapproved entertainment, dividends), transfer pricing adjustments, and deduction of prior-year tax losses within the 5-year carryforward limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head office administrative charges and management fees from the foreign parent must satisfy the real-benefit and arm's length tests; undeclared related-party fees are a compliance red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of gross amounts paid to non-residents (dividends, interest, royalties, technical and management service fees) and the WHT deducted at 10% or the applicable treaty rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SPC is the statutory withholding agent; non-resident recipients must submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate before treaty-reduced rates can be applied at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of all related-party transactions with the arm's length method applied (CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split); confirmation of Local File, Master File and CbCR obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent and shareholders must support mark-up and pricing policies with benchmarking studies; failure to prepare the Local File when aggregate related-party transactions exceed OMR 500,000 is a breach.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Tax Computation and Authorized Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income at 15% (or applicable progressive SME rates), tax credits, tax payable, loss utilization and the declaration signed by the SPC manager or authorized representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign shareholder-manager or the appointed resident manager must sign physically or via notarized e-power of attorney; e-filing must be authenticated with a valid OTA e-signature.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: OMR 100 for the first month plus OMR 20 per week or part-week thereafter, capped at OMR 500 per return. Late payment: 1% monthly interest (12% per annum) on the unpaid tax, plus administrative fines of up to 25% of the underpaid amount; repeated non-compliance may trigger criminal proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on gross dividends paid by the Omani SPC to a non-resident shareholder not operating through an Omani permanent establishment (Oman Income Tax Law Article 61). Dividends paid to resident shareholders are exempt from withholding. The 10% is deducted at source unless a double tax agreement provides a lower rate and the OTA holds the required documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The foreign shareholder must: (1) obtain an annual Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority; (2) submit the TRC plus a beneficial ownership declaration to the Oman Tax Authority through the SPC before the dividend payment date; (3) upon OTA validation of treaty entitlement, the SPC withholds at the reduced treaty rate; (4) if the full 10% was withheld, the non-resident may file a refund claim for the excess within the statutory limitation period, attaching the TRC, dividend resolution and audited financial statements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT is 10% on royalties and 10% on interest paid by the SPC to non-residents. Under Oman's double tax agreements, royalties are commonly reduced to 5%-10% and interest to 0%-10%, subject to beneficial ownership and minimum debt-holding period tests. Payments for technical and management services performed in Oman are also subject to the 10% statutory WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: OMR 500,000 aggregate value of controlled related-party transactions per tax year triggers a mandatory Local File; multinational groups with consolidated revenue exceeding OMR 75 million must prepare a Master File; groups with consolidated revenue exceeding OMR 300 million must file a Country-by-Country Report with the OTA within 12 months of the group year-end.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Oman does not apply a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Substance is instead enforced through tax residency rules based on the place of effective management, the general anti-abuse provisions, and licensing requirements. An Omani SPC manufacturing all-terrain military tactical vehicles must demonstrate genuine operational substance in Oman: physical production facilities, locally employed engineers and management, board decisions taken in Oman, payroll and active license compliance; otherwise the OTA may disregard the entity, shift POEM outside Oman, deny treaty benefits and recharacterize profits.
